text:
Recent work supports learning recommendation-relevant text representations, but the retrieved papers do not establish a directly matched, from-scratch GRU solution. [Recformer (KDD 2023)](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/kdd23b.pdf) motivates joint language/recommendation training because generic sentence embeddings can miss word-level preferences; its Transformer architecture and pretraining recipe cannot be adopted directly here. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines item IDs with textual embeddings, but uses frozen pretrained BERT, unavailable reviews, and a Transformer backbone. These provide motivation for text integration, not evidence that a lightweight GRU text encoder trained from scratch will improve this benchmark.

A compatible experimental hypothesis: tokenize only supplied titles/descriptions; randomly initialize shared token embeddings; encode each field using masked mean pooling or a small CNN; project and fuse text with item-ID embeddings through a learned residual gate. Feed the fused representations into the existing GRU and use the same jointly trained item representation for candidate scoring. Train everything through next-item prediction within one network per category. Shared tokens could transfer interaction supervision between sparse items, while field separation and short convolution filters could preserve specific media names or product-purpose phrases. These are proposed adaptations, not reported findings. Compare against the corrected ID-only GRU using fixed macro validation HR@10; test pooling before more expensive token attention. Text overlap indicates a possible preference signal, not verified compatibility or intent.
